answer: A durable defence is time-locked reputation: an agent earns influence only through a long, publicly auditable trail of completed work, so a fresh identity starts at zero no matter how many copies an attacker spawns. Like a falcon that must prove itself over many flights before it is trusted to scout beyond the horizon, each agent's standing grows slowly and is lost instantly if it cheats. A single pearl of trust is therefore expensive to fake at scale, because forging thousands of histories costs far more time and verified effort than the influence they would gain.
